mainTopic: Closing the עירוב debate; תפילה wording when שבת meets יום טוב, ראש חודש, or חול המועד; preparing on one day of יום טוב for the next; and עירובי תבשילין
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier debate. The גמרא pushes away a proof and rules like רבי, in the strict direction: no עירוב on יום טוב for the שבת that follows. Next, a ברייתא teaches how to pray when יום טוב falls on שבת. רבינא fixes the closing line to 'מְקַדֵּשׁ הַשַּׁבָּת, יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַזְּמַנִּים', and רב יוסף rules that way. A second ברייתא covers שבת on ראש חודש or חול המועד: יעלה ויבוא goes into רצה, and only מוסף is built around שבת. רב הונא rejects the pair who wanted that pattern in every תפילה. רב and רבא then allow setting an עירוב on the first day of a two-day יום טוב for the second, using a stipulation, but רבא limits this to עירובי תבשילין. A ברייתא forbids baking from one day of יום טוב to the next, and רבא rules like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר that you may fill the whole oven. Finally, the גמרא proves that without עירובי תבשילין both the person and his flour are forbidden. It then asks what happens if he baked anyway, an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier case was about the harm of forbidding what is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the proof brought just before, saying that a strict ruling there would itself be a קלקולא (a harmful mistake): forbidding the עירוב when it was really allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the harmful mistake [forbidding the עירוב when it was really allowed, so it proves nothing].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a discussion from before this section. It rejects a proof about making an עירוב on יום טוב for the שבת that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier case seemed to show what the final ruling is. The גמרא answers that ruling strictly there would itself be a קלקולא: if making the עירוב the day before was really allowed, forbidding it causes harm. So it cannot prove the general הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: that is / this is the same as
a mishap, a problem that goes wrong

phrases.english: That is the mishap.
phrases.notes: This answers a proof from just before this section. The case there was ruled that way only to avoid a problem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the earlier back-and-forth about the עירוב by rejecting the last proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the earlier case about the עירוב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That ruling was made to avoid a practical mishap. It was not a statement of the general הלכה.

steps.title: The final ruling follows רבי, in the strict direction
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רב חסדא in the name of רב הונא, rules like רבי and forbids making the עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב חסדא, who said it in the name of רב הונא: the הלכה follows רבי, and in the forbidding direction.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the proof has been pushed away, the גמרא gives the final ruling on the עירוב question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's opinion was reported in more than one version. This ruling takes the stricter one: on יום טוב you may not make an עירוב for the שבת that comes right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: the practical law follows (this opinion)
in the forbidding direction, stringently
רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put the משנה together

steps.whatToRemember: The עירוב discussion ends with the strict version of רבי's view: no עירוב on יום טוב for the following שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Chisda said that Rav Huna said:
The halacha follows Rabbi, and to forbid.
phrases.notes: 'To forbid' means making the עירוב on יום טוב for the next day's שבת is not allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the proof rejected, this gives the final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי, and stringently: one may not make an עירוב on יום טוב for the following שבת.

steps.title: How to pray the עמידה when יום טוב falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a debate. בית שמאי say eight ברכות, with separate ones for שבת and יום טוב. בית הלל say seven, with one combined middle ברכה. רבי adds that its closing line mentions both days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: when יום טוב falls on שבת, בית שמאי say you pray eight ברכות, saying one for שבת by itself and one for יום טוב by itself. בית הלל say you pray seven: you begin the middle ברכה with שבת, end it with שבת, and mention the holiness of the day (יום טוב) in the middle. רבי says you even close the ברכה with it: 'Who makes holy שבת, ישראל, and the seasons.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a ברייתא about how many ברכות to say when יום טוב and שבת fall on the same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the עמידה on שבת or יום טוב has seven ברכות: three at the start, one in the middle about the day, and three at the end. בית שמאי want a separate middle ברכה for each day, which makes eight. בית הלל keep seven by putting יום טוב inside the שבת ברכה. רבי goes further: יום טוב is mentioned in the closing line too, not only in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: the rabbis taught (this opens a ברייתא)
he prays eight / seven ברכות in the עמידה
by itself, as a separate ברכה
the holiness of the day, the middle ברכה about the special day
closes a ברכה with its final 'בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה' line

steps.confusionAlert: 'Seven' and 'eight' do not count the whole weekday שמונה עשרה. They count the ברכות of the special עמידה for שבת and יום טוב: three at the start, the middle one(s), and three at the end.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: a Yom Tov that falls on Shabbat,
Beit Shammai say: he prays eight [blessings],
[and he says] the one of Shabbat by itself,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: and the one of Yom Tov by itself.
And Beit Hillel say: he prays seven,

phrases.aramaic: מַתְחִיל בְּשֶׁל שַׁבָּת וּמְסַיֵּים בְּשֶׁל שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: he begins with Shabbat and ends with Shabbat,
and says the holiness of the day in the middle.
phrases.notes: 'The day' here means the יום טוב, which is tucked inside the שבת ברכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: he even closes with it:
"Who sanctifies Shabbat, Israel, and the seasons."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: how to word the תפילה when two special days fall together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: eight ברכות. בית הלל: seven, with יום טוב mentioned inside the שבת ברכה. רבי: the closing line also mentions both days.

steps.title: רבינא objects to a version that says ישראל make שבת holy
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recited the closing line as 'Who makes holy ישראל, and שבת, and the seasons.' רבינא objects: ישראל do not make שבת holy, because שבת is already holy by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא recited before רבינא: 'Who makes holy ישראל, and שבת, and the seasons.' רבינא said to him: Do ישראל make שבת holy? שבת is holy all by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone recites רבי's closing line in a different order, and רבינא challenges that order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting ישראל first sounds as if ישראל are the ones who make שבת holy. רבינא points out that שבת comes every seventh day on its own and is holy without anyone declaring it. So that order cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: a reciter of ברייתות taught in front of him
is that to say...? (a challenging question)
is already holy and stays holy on its own

phrases.english: A tanna recited before Ravina:
"Who sanctifies Israel and the Shabbat and the seasons."

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַטּוּ שַׁבָּת יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשִׁי לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: Is that to say Israel sanctify Shabbat?
phrases.notes: In this order the words read like 'Who makes ישראל holy, and they make שבת holy.'

phrases.english: But Shabbat is already sanctified and standing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges a different wording of רבי's closing line from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order 'ישראל, and שבת, and the seasons' in the closing line.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Putting ישראל before שבת suggests ישראל make שבת holy. But שבת is holy on its own.

steps.title: רבינא fixes the order: שבת comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the closing line should read 'Who makes holy שבת, ישראל, and the seasons.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: 'Who makes holy שבת, ישראל, and the seasons.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers his own challenge by moving שבת to the front of the closing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this order, ה׳ makes שבת holy directly. ה׳ also makes ישראל holy, and ישראל in turn make the seasons (יום טוב) holy, because the calendar is set by them. That fits how each kind of holiness actually works.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, say it this way (the text is corrected)
the seasons, meaning the ימים טובים

phrases.english: Rather, say: "Who sanctifies Shabbat, Israel, and the seasons."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge by correcting the wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The closing line could read 'ישראל, and שבת, and the seasons.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct wording is 'שבת, ישראל, and the seasons,' because שבת is holy on its own and does not depend on ישראל.

steps.title: רב יוסף rules like רבי, with רבינא's wording
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that the הלכה follows רבי, using the order רבינא gave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: the הלכה follows רבי, and as רבינא corrected it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on how to close the ברכה when יום טוב falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling combines two pieces. From רבי: you close the ברכה with both שבת and יום טוב. From רבינא: the order is שבת first, then ישראל, then the seasons.

keyTerms.meaning: and as he answered / corrected it

steps.whatToRemember: When יום טוב falls on שבת, the middle ברכה ends 'מְקַדֵּשׁ הַשַּׁבָּת, יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַזְּמַנִּים': like רבי, in רבינא's order.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the wording still said today when יום טוב falls on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: The halacha follows Rabbi,
and as Ravina resolved it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבינא's correction into the final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Close the ברכה with both days, as רבי says, in the order 'שבת, ישראל, and the seasons.'

steps.title: שבת on ראש חודש or חול המועד: where to add יעלה ויבוא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that in מעריב, שחרית, and מנחה you pray the usual seven ברכות and mention the special day in the ברכה of עבודה (רצה). If you forgot, you go back. רבי אליעזר says it goes in הודאה (מודים).
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: when שבת falls on ראש חודש or חול המועד, in ערבית, שחרית, and מנחה you pray seven ברכות and say something about the day's event in the ברכה of עבודה. If you did not say it, you are sent back. רבי אליעזר says: it goes in the ברכה of thanks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא about a different overlap: שבת together with ראש חודש or חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, unlike יום טוב, the special day does not get its own ending line in the regular תפילות. It is only mentioned as an addition, יעלה ויבוא. The תנא קמא places it in רצה, the ברכה about the Temple service. רבי אליעזר places it in מודים instead. Leaving it out is serious enough that you must repeat the תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: the middle days of פסח or סוכות
something about the day's event (יעלה ויבוא)
the ברכה about the Temple service, רצה
we send him back to say the תפילה again
the thanksgiving ברכה, מודים

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Shabbat that falls on Rosh Chodesh
or on Chol HaMoed,
for Arvit, Shacharit, and Mincha he prays seven,
and says something fitting the occasion in the Avodah blessing,
phrases.notes: This is יעלה ויבוא, added into רצה.

phrases.english: and if he did not say it, they send him back.
Rabbi Eliezer says: in the Thanksgiving blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּרֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from יום טוב on שבת to ראש חודש or חול המועד on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the regular תפילות you pray seven ברכות and add the special day in רצה, or in מודים according to רבי אליעזר. If you leave it out, you repeat the תפילה.

steps.title: How מוסף is built on these days
steps.stepSummary: In מוסף, the middle ברכה begins and ends with שבת, and the holiness of ראש חודש or the מועד is mentioned in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in מוסף, you begin with שבת and end with שבת, and say the holiness of the day in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains the special middle ברכה of מוסף on these days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מוסף is different because the day itself is its main subject. So the special day is not just a small addition here. Its holiness is said in the middle of the ברכה, wrapped inside the שבת opening and closing. This follows the same pattern בית הלל used for יום טוב on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the מוסף תפילה, said for the extra Temple offerings
begins ... and ends (the middle ברכה)

steps.whatToRemember: On שבת that is also ראש חודש or חול המועד, the regular תפילות add יעלה ויבוא. מוסף instead puts the day's holiness inside a ברכה that opens and closes with שבת.

phrases.english: And in the Musaf prayers he begins with Shabbat
and ends with Shabbat,
and says the holiness of the day in the middle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, now about מוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In מוסף, the middle ברכה opens and closes with שבת, and the holiness of ראש חודש or the מועד is said in the middle.

steps.title: A dissenting pair: every seven-ברכה תפילה is built around שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא say that whenever you say seven ברכות, the middle ברכה starts and ends with שבת, and the special day goes in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל, the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, say: Any time a person must say seven ברכות, he begins with שבת, ends with שבת, and mentions the holiness of the day in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now brings a second opinion that argues with the first opinion from Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, the first opinion said that in מעריב, שחרית, and מנחה you say the normal שבת תפילה and mention the special day in רצה. Step 8 described the מוסף pattern, where the middle ברכה starts and ends with שבת and the special day goes in the middle. This pair says to use that same מוסף pattern in every seven-ברכה תפילה, not only in מוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Required to say seven ברכות (the שבת עמידה of מעריב, שחרית, and מנחה)
Wherever, in every case
In the middle

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, say:
Wherever one is required to say seven blessings,
phrases.notes: He means the תפילות of a שבת that falls on ראש חודש or חול המועד: מעריב, שחרית, and מנחה, not only מוסף.

phrases.english: he begins with that of Shabbat
and concludes with that of Shabbat
and says the holiness of the day in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the מוסף pattern from Step 8 and applies it to all seven-ברכה תפילות, which argues with the first opinion in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In every seven-ברכה תפילה on such a day, the middle ברכה opens and closes with שבת, with the special day mentioned in the middle.

steps.title: רב הונא rules against the pair
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the הלכה does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The הלכה is not like that pair.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the final ruling. We do not follow the pair from Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the pair is rejected, the first opinion of Step 7 stands. In מעריב, שחרית, and מנחה you say the normal שבת תפילה and mention the special day in רצה. Only מוסף uses the begin-and-end-with-שבת pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law does not follow
Pair (of חכמים who share one opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows the first opinion. The special day goes into רצה in regular תפילות, and the 'begin and end with שבת' structure is only for מוסף.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The halakha is not in accordance with that pair.
phrases.notes: The 'pair' is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל from the line just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument between Step 7's first opinion and Step 9's pair.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows the first opinion of the ברייתא, not the pair.

steps.title: רב allows setting עירובי תחומין on the first day of יום טוב for the second
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that on the first day of a two-day יום טוב, a person may set an עירובי תחומין for the second day, using a stipulation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: A person may set an עירובי תחומין on one day of יום טוב for the next day, and make a stipulation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. Outside ארץ ישראל יום טוב is kept for two days out of doubt, and רב teaches how someone can set an עירוב on the first day for the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one of the two days is really יום טוב. He stipulates: if today is יום טוב, tomorrow is a weekday and I don't need an עירוב; if today is a weekday, then this עירוב works for tomorrow. Either way, he never sets an עירוב on a real יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: An עירוב that lets a person walk farther than the usual limit on שבת or יום טוב
Places / sets down (the עירוב)
Literally 'for its friend', meaning the next day of יום טוב
Makes a stipulation (a condition)

steps.confusionAlert: He is not setting an עירוב on a definite יום טוב. The stipulation works because of the doubt about which of the two days is really יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
A person may place an eiruv for joining boundaries
on one Festival day for the next,
phrases.notes: He means the first day of יום טוב for the second day, which is kept outside ארץ ישראל because of a doubt.

phrases.english: and stipulate.
phrases.notes: The condition is: if today is the real יום טוב, I don't need the עירוב; if tomorrow is, let this count for tomorrow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב מַנִּיחַ אָדָם עֵירוּבֵי תְחוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about עירובין on a two-day יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first day of a two-day יום טוב, one may set an עירובי תחומין for the second day by making a stipulation.

steps.title: רבא allows setting עירובי תבשילין on the first day of יום טוב for the second
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the same rule as רב, but about עירובי תבשילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A person may set an עירובי תבשילין on one day of יום טוב for the next day, and make a stipulation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a parallel statement about a different kind of עירוב, the one that lets you cook on יום טוב for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stipulation works the same way. If today is a weekday and tomorrow is יום טוב, this עירוב lets him cook tomorrow for שבת. If today is יום טוב, tomorrow is a weekday and he may cook normally. The גמרא will next compare רב's rule with רבא's.

keyTerms.meaning: An עירוב of cooked food that allows cooking on יום טוב for the שבת right after it

phrases.english: Rava said:
A person may place an eiruv for joining cooked foods
on one Festival day for the next,
and stipulate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא מַנִּיחַ אָדָם עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel ruling to Step 11, for עירובי תבשילין instead of עירובי תחומין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first day of a two-day יום טוב, one may set an עירובי תבשילין for the second day by making a stipulation.

steps.title: Comparing the two rulings: one is a קל וחומר, the other is limited
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב, who allows עירובי תחומין, would surely allow עירובי תבשילין. רבא, who allows עירובי תבשילין, would not allow עירובי תחומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who allows עירובי תחומין would surely allow עירובי תבשילין. But the one who allows עירובי תבשילין would not allow עירובי תחומין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out how רב and רבא relate to each other. This sets up the question 'why?' in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עירובי תחומין is the stricter case. So whoever allows it would allow the easier case of עירובי תבשילין. רבא spoke only about the easier case, so he would not allow the stricter one.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who said
All the more so

phrases.english: The one who said joining of boundaries —
all the more so joining of cooked foods,
but the one who said joining of cooked foods —
however, joining of boundaries, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר עֵירוּבֵי תְחוּמִין כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares Steps 11 and 12 and shows that רב's ruling covers more than רבא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's permission includes עירובי תבשילין; רבא's permission does not include עירובי תחומין.

steps.title: Why is עירובי תחומין stricter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא would allow עירובי תבשילין but not עירובי תחומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of עירוב use the same stipulation, so the difference needs a reason. The question asks what makes עירובי תחומין harder to allow.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the difference drawn in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why עירובי תחומין may not be set on the first day of יום טוב even though עירובי תבשילין may.

steps.title: You may not acquire a resting place on a day of rest
steps.stepSummary: The answer: an עירובי תחומין acquires a resting place (שביתה), and acquiring a שביתה on a day of rest is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because acquiring a resting place on a day of rest is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: עירובי תחומין is different because it works by acquiring a שביתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירובי תחומין works by acquiring a new 'home base' (שביתה) for the day, which is a kind of acquiring. That may not be done on a day of rest, even with a stipulation. עירובי תבשילין does not acquire a שביתה, so this problem does not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: To acquire
The place a person sets as his resting place for the day. His walking limits are measured from it.
A day of rest, here including יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: רב allows both kinds of עירוב on the first day of יום טוב with a stipulation. רבא allows only עירובי תבשילין, because acquiring a שביתה on a day of rest is not allowed.

phrases.english: That acquiring a residence on a day of rest is not allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עירובי תחומין acquires a שביתה, and acquiring a שביתה on a day of rest is not allowed. עירובי תבשילין does not involve this.

steps.title: No baking from one day of יום טוב for the next
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may not bake on one day of יום טוב for the other day. A pot of meat or a barrel of water may be filled completely, but baking is limited to what is needed that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One may not bake on one day of יום טוב for the next day. But truly they said: a woman may fill a whole pot with meat even though she needs only one piece, and a baker may fill a whole barrel of water even though he needs only one jug. But when it comes to baking, he bakes only what he needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about preparing food on the first day of יום טוב for the second day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking for the next day is normally forbidden. Filling a pot with extra meat, or a barrel with extra water, is allowed, because it is all done in one act with no added work. Baking is different: each loaf is extra work, so you may bake only what you need today.

keyTerms.meaning: Bake
'Truly they said': introduces an accepted, fixed rule
Cooking pot
Baker
Small jug

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the meat and water cases mean you may cook for tomorrow. You may add extra only because it is all one act done for today's need. Extra baking is separate work, so it is not allowed.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not bake on one day of יום טוב for the other.
Truly they said:
A woman may fill the whole pot with meat,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה אֶלָּא לַחֲתִיכָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: even though she needs only one piece.
A baker may fill a barrel of water,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ אֶלָּא לְקִיתוֹן אֶחָד.
phrases.english: even though he needs only one jug.
But to bake:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אוֹפֶה אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁצָּרִיךְ לוֹ.
phrases.english: he bakes only what he needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין אוֹפִין מִיּוֹם טוֹב לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of preparing on one day of יום טוב for the next day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No baking from one day of יום טוב for the next. A full pot of meat or barrel of water is allowed, but baking is limited to what is needed that day.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר allows filling the whole oven
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says a woman may fill the whole oven with bread, because bread bakes better when the oven is full.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: A woman may fill the whole oven with bread, because bread bakes well when the oven is full.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagrees about baking and allows a full oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is that the extra loaves also help today's bread, since a full oven bakes better. So the extra baking is not only for tomorrow. It also improves the food for today.

keyTerms.meaning: Oven
Bread
Bakes well

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
A woman may fill the whole oven with bread,
because bread bakes well
when the oven is full.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion within the same ברייתא about baking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A whole oven may be filled with bread, because a full oven improves the baking.

steps.title: רבא rules like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא decides the argument in the ברייתא: one may fill the whole oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the disagreement from the last two steps. In practice, one may fill the oven with bread on יום טוב, even if some of it will be left for later.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling follows (this opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: No baking from one day of יום טוב to the next, but you may fill the whole oven, because it makes today's bread better. The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One may fill the whole oven with bread on יום טוב.

steps.title: Is only the person forbidden, or his flour too?
steps.stepSummary: Someone did not set an עירובי תבשילין. Is only he forbidden to cook for שבת, or is his flour also forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Someone who did not set an עירובי תבשילין: is he forbidden and his flour forbidden too? Or perhaps he is forbidden, but his flour is not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about someone who forgot to set an עירובי תבשילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an עירובי תבשילין, a person may not cook on יום טוב for שבת. The question is whether this rule is placed on the person only, or also on his food. If it is on the food, nobody could bake his flour for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They asked': a question raised in the בית מדרש
Food set aside before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת
Is forbidden
His flour
Or perhaps

phrases.english: They asked:
One who did not set an eruv tavshilin:
is he forbidden and his flour forbidden,
phrases.notes: Forbidden here means it may not be used to cook or bake on יום טוב for שבת.

phrases.english: or perhaps:
he is forbidden but his flour is not forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מִי שֶׁלֹּא הִנִּיחַ עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about עירובי תבשילין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban from not setting an עירובי תבשילין apply only to the person, or also to his flour?

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference the question makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the question matters in practice. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before trying to answer, the גמרא wants to know what real case depends on this question.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference comes out of this?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what practical case depends on the question in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what practical case do the two sides of the question lead to different results?

steps.title: Whether he must transfer his flour to others
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether he must give his flour to others so they can bake for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is about transferring his flour to others. If you say he is forbidden and his flour is forbidden, he must transfer his flour to others. If you say he is forbidden but his flour is not, he does not need to transfer his flour to others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the practical difference: does he need to give his flour to someone else so it can be baked for him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the flour itself is forbidden, others may bake it only after it becomes theirs, so he must transfer it to them. If only the person is forbidden, others may bake his own flour for him, and no transfer is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: To transfer ownership
If you say
Other people

phrases.english: For transferring his flour to others.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ הוּא נֶאֱסָר וְקִמְחוֹ נֶאֱסָר —
phrases.english: If you say he is forbidden and his flour is forbidden,
he needs to transfer his flour to others.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ הוּא נֶאֱסָר וְאֵין קִמְחוֹ נֶאֱסָר —
phrases.english: And if you say he is forbidden but his flour is not forbidden,
he does not need to transfer his flour to others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is whether he must transfer ownership of his flour to others so they may bake it for him.

steps.title: So what is the law?
steps.stepSummary: With the practical difference clear, the גמרא asks again: what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the question, now asking for a real answer. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know what depends on it, the גמרא asks for a ruling: is the flour forbidden or not?

keyTerms.meaning: What (is the law)?

phrases.english: What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question of step 19 and asks for an answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, without an עירובי תבשילין, the flour is forbidden too, or only the person.

steps.title: A ברייתא says he must transfer his flour to others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. It says a person without עירובי תבשילין may not bake, cook or insulate food, for himself or for others, and others may not cook for him. His solution is to give his flour to others so they can bake and cook for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who did not set עירובי תבשילין may not bake, cook or insulate food, not for himself and not for others. Others may also not bake or cook for him. What should he do? He transfers ownership of his flour to others, and they bake and cook for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question from Step 22: is his flour also forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says others may not bake for him while the flour is still his. Only after he gives the flour away may they bake. This detail is the key evidence, and the next step spells it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This introduces a source brought as a proof.
The cooked food set aside before יום טוב so that one may cook on יום טוב for the שבת that follows.
Insulate. Wrapping food to keep it hot.
Transfers ownership of something to someone else.
His flour.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who did not set an eruv tavshilin,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יֹאפֶה וְלֹא יְבַשֵּׁל וְלֹא יַטְמִין,
phrases.english: may not bake, nor cook, nor insulate food,
neither for himself nor for others.
And others may not bake or cook for him.
What should he do?
He transfers his flour to others,
and they bake for him and cook for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question restated in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the flour of someone who did not set עירובי תבשילין is also forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא requiring him to transfer his flour to others before they bake for him.

steps.title: Conclusion: both he and his flour are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא requires the flour to be transferred. From this the גמרא concludes that the flour itself is forbidden, not only the person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: he is forbidden and his flour is forbidden. Indeed, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא and accepts it as the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose only the person were forbidden. Then others could simply bake with his flour while it still belonged to him. The ברייתא requires the flour to be transferred first, so the flour must be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. When it is repeated at the end, it means the proof is accepted.
Is forbidden.

steps.whatToRemember: A person who did not set עירובי תבשילין is forbidden to cook, and his flour is forbidden too. Others can bake for him only after he transfers the flour to them.

phrases.english: Learn from this:
he is forbidden and his flour is forbidden,
indeed, learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ הוּא נֶאֱסָר וְקִמְחוֹ נֶאֱסָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in Step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the person and his flour are forbidden. That is why he must transfer the flour to others.

steps.title: New question: what if he went ahead and baked?
steps.stepSummary: A new question is raised. If someone without עירובי תבשילין broke the rule and baked anyway, what is the law about the food?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If he transgressed and baked, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. What happens after the fact if someone baked without עירובי תבשילין?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about what he may do from the start. Now the question is about the result once the wrong thing was already done. Is the food he baked allowed or forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (the חכמים).
He transgressed and baked. He did it even though he should not have.
What? Here it means: what is the law?

phrases.english: They asked:
If he transgressed and baked, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the settled question to a new one about the case after the fact.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether food baked without עירובי תבשילין is permitted after the fact.

steps.title: Bringing the same ברייתא to answer the new question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again, focusing on its solution: transfer the flour to others so they can bake for him. It is about to draw an inference about the case where he baked anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who did not set עירובי תבשילין, what should he do? He transfers his flour to others, and the others bake and cook for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא again, this time to try to answer the new question. This step sets up an inference that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives only one way out: transferring the flour. The גמרא is preparing to learn from this one solution what the law is when he bakes on his own. The actual inference comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: How should he act? This is the ברייתא's way of giving a practical solution.
They bake.

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same ברייתא as in Step 23, but it is now brought for a different purpose: to answer the new question about baking after the fact.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who did not set an eruv tavshilin,
what should he do?
He transfers his flour to others,
and the others bake for him and cook for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא again to try to answer the question raised in Step 25.
steps.raayaObject: The law of food baked without עירובי תבשילין after the fact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's only solution is transferring the flour to others. The inference from this follows in the next lines.
